rationale:
bugs_open/305. The owner read three live directory pages, quoted two sentences built on define-by-negation ("The registry shows you what's possible, not what survives production"; "A model directory tells you which agents exist. It doesn't tell you how they...") and ruled that "that sort of copy never leaves this framework again".

WHY THIS IS CODE AND NOT ANOTHER PROMPT RULE. The rule already exists and does not hold. The v2 house voice says "Say what a thing IS rather than what it is not"; migration 228 shipped the same rule on 2026-07-27 and its own header records that it "did not work" because "a rule competing with that much context loses". The fleet_copy_quality lane's controlled ablation concluded "A rule can only name a form. What goes wrong is an instinct" and "prescriptions become tics". Measured 2026-08-19 over 1,503 page-content-writer calls (08-13..19): the construction is in 42% of sections (x_not_y), and the writer produced it again for the complained-of site on 08-19 at 18:26-18:32Z. So the prompt keeps its rule and a mechanical check goes behind it.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT TODAY. datahelpers/voicetells.go:151 strawmanCommaRe requires a trailing ", but" - it matches "not X, but Y" only, which is 1.5% of sections and neither of the owner's sentences. It runs post-deploy, and only for the 9 of 43 sites with voice_gate.enabled. Nothing at all sits between the writer's generate_content and render_section.

WHAT THIS CHANGE IS. (1) The family as a pure scanner shared by both ends, so the post-deploy check and the writer-seam gate cannot disagree about what the fault IS (the CQ-020 precedent). (2) A default-ON annotation in render_component so the COUNT exists for every LLM-authored section from every writer, wired or not - "a gate a workflow author can forget to wire is a comment" (save_page_meta_description_action.go:44-48). (3) A new action, rewrite_negations, with its own ActionInputSpec, that repairs by asking for SENTENCE REPLACEMENTS and splicing them in Go. It never fails the step.

THREE SUB-DESIGNS MEASUREMENT REFUTED FIRST, because they are the reasons the shape is what it is. (a) "Re-ask for the whole section, keep whichever attempt scores lower" ADOPTS DISPLACEMENT: in the same corpus "instead of" is 5.9%, "isn't just/a" 6.4%, "more than just" 10.8%, so a rewrite to "X instead of Y" scores zero on the five shapes and wins. Hence per-replacement acceptance against a neighbour set, with rejections logged. (b) "Exempt any hit whose phrase is verbatim in the rendered prompt" is FATAL: the literal string "rather than" is in every rendered writer prompt (house voice x6 plus STRICT RULE 19), so the whole 43% arm would be silently exempt. Hence sentence-scoped exemption against brief-supplied fields only. (c) Quoting the house-voice rule in the repair prompt re-supplies the form ("the example is the instruction; the rule is commentary"), so the repair prompt carries no rule text and no example of the banned shape.

SCOPE HELD DELIBERATELY NARROW. Brief-supplied sentences and regulatory negations are EXEMPT - counted, not rewritten - because "a site's own voice specification outranks these rules" is the house voice's own first sentence, and because rewriting "not financial advice" would be a compliance harm dressed as a style fix. That means this change deliberately does NOT clean the three pages the owner named: their tagline is supplied by the site's content_direction (1,369 rendered prompts -> 409 responses). The brief edit and rerender belong to the site's own lane and they have been told.

plan.summary: Add the define-by-negation family as a pure, shared scanner; make the existing voice gate use it (it was blind to the shape the owner complained about); count it on every rendered LLM section; and add one new action that repairs the sentences beyond a per-PAGE budget of two, or any in a headline-class field, by splicing model-supplied replacements that pass a displacement and fact-preservation check. Opt-in per step, default OFF, enabled by a held migration on page-content-writer only.

edits.rationale: The family, pure and shared. Five shapes: x_not_y, not_x_but_y, staccato, rather_than, negative_reveal. Each hit carries its containing SENTENCE and the byte offsets that address the RAW field value, because the repair splices by exact substring and a sentence recovered from stripped text is not a substring of the field it came from. Sentence edges are trimmed of whole HTML tags so a rich_text paragraph reads as prose. negative_reveal is the owner's second quoted example and is invisible to every single-sentence pattern.

The displacement set, as a SEPARATE class that can never trip the gate and can only reject a rewrite. Without it the repair passes by moving the problem, which is the estate's measured 'a prohibition displaces a problem rather than solving it'. Each pattern is narrow enough that it cannot fire on an ordinary factual comparison: 'more than 30 agents' must not count, so the just/merely/simply qualifier is required. The em dash is included because the house voice bans it outright, so a rewrite that introduces one has traded one violation for another.
edits.sketch:
instead_of | more_than_just | isnt_just | is_not_just | unlike | as_opposed_to | far_from | no_longer_just | without_being | em_dash
{"more_than_just", regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\bmore than (?:just|merely|simply)\b`)},  // NOT bare 'more than'

edits.rationale: Sentence-scoped exemption, against brief-supplied text ONLY, plus a regulatory allowlist. A prompt-wide test exempts every 'rather than' in the estate. The core is tried at 4, 3 and 2 words either side, widest first, because the writer EXTENDS a supplied phrase: the brief says 'deployed to production in days, not months' and the writer emitted '...in days, not months on Kubernetes.', so a single wide window reports NOT-supplied for a phrase the brief demonstrably handed over. The 18-character floor on the normalised form is what stops it narrowing to 's, not m' and exempting everything.

The whole reason a repair here cannot quietly make things worse; it fails CLOSED, so any doubt keeps the original sentence. protectFrom is the offset of the construction being removed: facts BEFORE it are the claim and must survive, facts after it are the contrasted alternative the rewrite is meant to drop. That asymmetry is the only way 'preserve every number' can coexist with 'delete the contrast' - 'We run 1,600 orchestrations a day, not 12' must keep 1,600 and may lose the 12.
edits.sketch: reject: empty | unchanged | gutted (<40%) | ballooned (>220%) | still_<shape> | displaced_<neighbour> | dropped_figure (before protectFrom) | invented_figure | dropped_link | markup_changed (tag multiset) | invented_name (capitalised token absent from the original)

edits.rationale: The existing strawman arm was blind to the shape the owner complained about. It now calls the shared scanner, so the post-deploy check, the meta-description gate and the new writer-seam gate cannot answer 'is this the fault?' differently - the same sharing argument as ScanVoiceTells between the emit side and the revalidator. ONE finding per SHAPE per block carrying that shape's count, not one per hit: per-hit findings would flag almost every page and tell a human nothing. 'rather than' is excluded from the per-hit path entirely and becomes a page-level DENSITY (contrast_density, default 2, long-form 4) mirroring triad_density, because it is present in 43% of sections and the house voice permits a contrasting pair once or twice per page.

The count goes where it cannot be forgotten. Every LLM-authored section from every writer passes through this action, so the annotation makes the fault MEASURABLE fleet-wide even where the repair is not wired - and it changes no output. Same result-surfacing pattern as migration 474's stripped_markdown_fields: pod logs rotate in minutes, collected_data is the durable record. Deliberately NOT a refusal: this action's existing refusal path loses the section, and style is softer than truth (the voice_tells severity precedent).

The repair, as its OWN action rather than a key on execute_llm_prompt. That action has 66 carriers and no ActionInputSpec, so the RFC_022 optional-key budget cannot see keys added to it; and a prose-quality rewrite is writer behaviour, not transport behaviour, in an action that also serves council seats and classifiers. It asks for sentence REPLACEMENTS and splices them in Go: a whole-section re-ask costs ~5x more (measured 11,009 in / 2,126 out tokens per writer call, 0 cached prompts) and can truncate, drop a key or change a type, which loses the section at this pipeline's required-field refusal. Per-PAGE budget of 2 carried in CollectedData because a per-section threshold cannot enforce a per-page standard - six sections at one hit each is six on the page and every one passes. Never fails the step; one llm_call_log row per repair with a RETRY (bugs_open/305 marker.
edits.sketch:
scan -> exempt (brief-supplied/regulatory) -> page budget from CollectedData["__copy_gate"] ->
ONE call asking for {"replacements":[{field,from,to}]} ->
AcceptNegationRewrite per replacement -> splice `to` over the verbatim `from` IN PLACE on
generated_content.result (the map the renderer will read) -> stamp out["__copy_gate"] =
{hits_before,hits_after,rewritten,rejected:[{field,reason}],exempt,page_hits}
The repair prompt carries the positive instruction ONLY - no rule text, no example of the banned form.

edits.rationale: The entire enablement surface: the action is default OFF because nothing names it until this runs. Anchored on each step's ACTION value and needle-gated exactly as migration 474 is, so a moved path means 0 rows and a loud RAISE rather than an orphan key, and a re-run is a legitimate 0-row no-op. It ships as _HOLD because it rewires the step CHAIN: applied before the image, the chain names a step the running binary cannot resolve. _HOLD is excluded from the auto-apply sweep and still listed.

voicetells.go:151 strawmanCommaRe = `(?i)\bnot (?:just |merely |simply |about )?[^.;:]{2,50},\s*but\b` - requires the trailing ', but', so it matches neither sentence the owner quoted.

MEASURED 2026-08-19 over llm_call_log, agent_type='page-content-writer', success, 2026-08-13..19, 1,503 calls: x_not_y in 631 (42%), >=2 in 208 (14%); rather_than 646 (43%); not_x_but_y 23 (1.5%); negative reveal 168 (11%); a headline-class field carrying x_not_y 209 (14%). Displacement baselines in the same corpus: instead of 5.9%, isn't just/a 6.4%, more than (just) 10.8%, em dash 0.5%.

MEASURED 2026-08-19: mean writer call 11,009 input / 2,126 output tokens, 0 cached prompts (the template carries no CACHE_BREAKPOINT), 1,503 calls/week ~ 215/day - so a whole-section re-ask is ~$0.072 against ~$0.0135 for the replacement patch.

save_page_meta_description_action.go:44-48: the checks "are enforced HERE, in the action, rather than in the calling workflow, because a gate a workflow author can forget to wire is a comment (owner ruling 2026-08-02 sect 2, the same reasoning as overwrite_existing)".

House voice (agent_default_configs.voice_style_block, v2, live): "A site's own voice specification outranks these rules wherever the two disagree" and "A very short closing sentence or a matched contrasting pair is earned once or twice per page at most" - the source of both the exemption rule and the budget of 2.

bugs_open/305 root-cause block, MEASURED 2026-08-19: the canonical tagline 'in days, not months' appears in 1,348 rendered prompts and 408 responses, while 'not a sales process' appears in 0 prompts and 35 responses - so supplied phrases transfer verbatim AND the model also produces the construction unprompted.
plan.risks:
1. DISPLACEMENT ADOPTED SILENTLY is the failure mode that would make this change worse than nothing. Mitigated by per-replacement rejection against the neighbour set, and every rejection is logged with its reason so displacement becomes measurable rather than inferred. Residual: the same instinct in a grammar nobody listed. A reviewer should check the neighbour list for a shape it misses.
2. A REGULATORY OR BRIEF-SUPPLIED NEGATION REWRITTEN. Mitigated by sentence-scoped exemption, the regulatory allowlist, and the fact-preservation checks. Residual: a novel disclaimer wording that the allowlist does not name. A reviewer should check the allowlist against the live specs of the regulated sites (loanzy.uk, lendzy.co.uk, vetcomparison.uk).
3. THE PER-PAGE BUDGET DEPENDS ON CollectedData PERSISTING ACROSS LOOP ITERATIONS. Read from the loop injection design (loop_actions.go) and the in-place mutation precedents (ai_actions.go, v3_site_actions.go), but NOT yet proven at runtime - it is stated as a canary to run after the roll, not as a fact. If it does not hold, the gate degrades to per-section (headline hits still repaired) rather than failing.
4. THE 43% ARM MAY BE TOO BROAD. 'rather than' is either a real fleet-wide tic or evidence the pattern is too wide. It is a density (not a per-hit finding) in the post-deploy check for exactly that reason, and the rejection log will settle it within a week of traffic. The owning lane has been asked the question directly.
5. COST AND LATENCY: ~43% of sections re-asked once at ~$0.0135 each, ~$1.2-1.7/day at today's 215 sections/day; with the bugs_open/119 re-ask also firing, up to three calls on one section. If anyone later changes this to re-ask for the whole section, that becomes ~$200/month and materially slower page builds.
6. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it does not clean the three pages the owner named (their tagline is brief-supplied and therefore exempt), and it holds five named FORMS rather than promising the instinct is gone. Both are stated to the owner and to the three affected lanes rather than discovered later.
